title: Month-end close
purpose: The bookkeeper's month-end checklist; the check that caught the missing money.
facts: Close in the first three working days of the next month; nine ordered steps.
Open orders need a reason; over 60 days are reported to slot 2 (ERP mess kind 4: one order at west open five months, two more over sixty days).
Till differences are summed by shop and by closer (how the 19 short days of slot F1 showed).

Void list with voider and payment; discounts over 10 % have an approver; no cash orders on the Walk-in customer; supplier credits; statements on the first working day; payroll hours; sales tax by the 20th.
Steps 2 to 5 were added or tightened in the month of {{@discount_rule}}.

list_items.item: Open orders. Every order still open from before the last week of the month is either finished and invoiced, or has a reason. I ask each shop manager for the reasons. An order open more than 60 days is reported to Claire.

Till counts. For each shop: every day has a count, and the differences for the month are added up by shop and by the person who closed. A few dollars either way is ordinary. I look for the same name short again and again.

Voids. The list of every voided order, with who voided it and whether a payment had been taken. Since {{@discount_rule|date}}, a paid order voided by anyone but a shop manager is reported the same day.
Discounts. Every bill with more than 10 % off has an approver. Claire receives the same list each Friday.
Cash orders on the Walk-in customer. There should be none.
Supplier statements against what we received: credits for returns and cores are there, or I ask Marcus.
Company-account statements go out on the first working day: Statements and receivables.
Payroll hours for the last period: Payroll hours.
Sales tax return, filed and paid by the 20th.

new_facts: Orders open more than 60 days are reported to slot 2 (matches the "over sixty days" of S15 kind 4).
Sales tax return by the 20th of the following month (Tennessee's due date as generally known; to be re-read on the state's page with the tax rows of the ledger).
